episodes.187108: A series of frontal systems with a weak subtropical tap led to widespread rainfall and nuisance flooding across the Bay Area and Central Coast.
episodes.187185: Following the departure of a storm which brought light to moderate precipitation to the  area between the morning of January 20 and the early afternoon of January 21, a second system moved through central California between the late evening of January 21 and the afternoon of January 22. This system produced three quarters to an inch and a half of rainfall over Merced County and a half inch to an inch of liquid precipitation the the Sierra Nevada with the snow level around 8000 feet. Much of the remainder of the San Joaquin Valley and the Tehachapi Mountains picked up between a half inch and an inch of rainfall which produced some localized flooding.
episodes.187884: Historic flooding occurred on January 22nd. Heavy rainfall occurred between 8 am and noon across western San Diego county. The heaviest rainfall occurred between 9 am and 11 am in the east side of the city of San Diego in Encanto and Lemon Grove to Spring Valley. Rainfall rates were observed at 1.5 to 2.5 inches in 60 minutes and resulted in 1000 year return intervals. Over 200 water rescues at homes, streets and in water channels were performed by San Diego Fire and Rescue. FEMA found 1000 homes damaged in the following weeks and 600 were declared major damage resulting in up to 31 million in damage claims and displaced residents, including 1200 households, in temporary shelters for several months. San Diego County EOC was activated on January 22 and remained activated at a low level into May 2024. The areas flooded the most were Mountain View, Encanto, Valencia Park, Shelltown, Southcrest, and Lincoln Park.
episodes.188343: Two storms brought heavy mountain snow with mountain travel delays and chain restrictions, widespread rain with flooding impacts, and thunderstorms to the area around the third week of January.
episodes.188372: A shortwave trough moving across the Desert Southwest combined with well-above normal moisture, with precipitable water values peak at 1.0-1.2, resulted in a large swath of rain with embedded thunderstorms moving across portions of southeast CA during the late morning and afternoon hours on the 22nd. Rainfall rates ranged between 0.10-0.50 according to doppler radar estimates, resulting in total amounts of between 0.5-1.25 within a period of three hours. The rainfall was enough to result in areas of flooding , causing several road closures. High water levels along the New River in Calexico caused damage to an Improvement Project that was being performed along the river itself. A state of emergency was declared for both the city of El Centro and Calexico according to the Imperial County Emergency Manager.
episodes.188373: A shortwave trough moving across the Desert Southwest combined with well-above normal moisture, with precipitable water values peaking at 1.0-1.2, resulted in a large swath of rain with embedded thunderstorms moving across portions of southeast CA and southwest AZ during the afternoon hours on the 22nd. Rainfall rates with this band ranged between 0.10-0.50 according to doppler radar estimates, resulting in total amounts of between 1-1.25 within a period of three hours. The rainfall was enough to result in areas of flooding.
episodes.188592: An upper-level trough remained nearly stationary over the western US resulting in southwesterly flow over Texas. A stationary boundary stretched across central Texas with anomalously moist air south of the boundary. A series of shortwave troughs moved through the upper pattern generating several rounds of locally heavy rain over three days. There was also some large hail.

Trained spotter report of 6 inches of water flowing over a roadway 30 feet wide. Water was up to the bumpers of cars.
CalTrans report of flooding across the entire freeway at SR-94 West and I-805. Rainfall of 2-3 inches in 60 to 90 minutes between 930 and 1100 am from heavy rainfall and thunderstorms.
I-5 North/Leucadia South slow lane had standing water and dirt following a landslide in the area. One inch of rain fell in the prior 3 hours.
Flooding observed in intersections with ponding water in some residential areas.

Roadway flooding was reported at CA Highway 1 Southbound at Scott Creek. Water was reported across both lanes and vehicles were hydroplaning in the area.
Roadway flooding observed at SR-163 N and Quince Street.

A vehicle was stuck in water at the on-ramp of I-5 North and 28th Street in National City, persons were trapped inside. Rainfall rates in at the time of report were 1.30 inches per hour.||Northbound I-15 at Main Street was fully closed around 1:30 PM due to flooding, and drivers were at a standstill in the flooded roadways.
The off-ramp at SR-163 and Ash Street was closed due to major flooding. Rainfall rates in the area were measured between 0.80 and 1.30 inches in one hour.

CalTrans report of significant flooding near I-805 South and Imperial Avenue and Market Street in Encanto. Large debris and several vehicles were video taped moving downstream on Chollas Creek near Jacob Center and Chollas View, starting at the park. The light rail double train tracks were undercut and severely damaged. Concrete lining in the channel was completely removed and chain link fencing destroyed by debris and flash flooding. Numerous homes in Encanto were flooded out and damaged. FEMA estimated up to 600 homes in this area had major flood damage. This area had rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour and 3 inches in around 90 minutes. Spring Valley ALERT recorded 1000 year rainfall return interval with 2.45 inches in 60 minutes and 3.15 inches in 2 hours. San Diego Fire and rescue reported just over 200 water rescues. There worse areas and were 1200 households were displaced from floods included Mountain View, Encanto, Valencia Park, Shelltown, Southcrest, and Lincoln Park.
CalTrans reported flooding on the Witch Creek Bridge on Highway 79.
SR-15 South and Adams Ave had standing water. 1.0-1.5 inches of rain fell in the area in the previous 3 hours.

Fox5 in San Diego reported that two people, 46 year old female and 48 year old male, were found deceased, drowning in a creek in Santee, near the intersection of Prospect Avenue and Cuyamaca Road. Exactly how and when the deceased were swept into the creek is unknown.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that flooded FM 795 at the Liveoak Branch Creek crossing east of Gonzales.
Water was reported across all lanes of Eastbound Interstate 580.
The offramp from US Highway 101 North to California Route 1 North was closed due to flooding.

Village Elementary School on Coronado had floodwater several inches deep occur indoors. County officials evacuated students around midday from the ground floor to upstairs classrooms. At least 16 businesses on Orange Avenue sustained flood damage. The PAWS of Coronado animal shelter was flooded, and animals were removed from the garage and transported to other locations. Sewer systems were severely impacted, and residents in the County Club area were urged to not conduct any activity that would discharge water into the drainage system.
California Highway Patrol reported Reed Rd. was closed due to flooding between County Line Rd. and Cecil Ave.
All westbound lanes on SR-78 from College Blvd to El Camino Real were closed due to flooding.

San Diego River reached 11.3 feet at USGS Fashion Mall gauge. Flooding in the area was significant including full closure and barricades with flowing water over all crossings, Qualcomm Way, Mission Center road, Fashion Valley road, Camino del Este, Ward road, and Mission road. San Diego fire reported 25 water rescues in the region and tributaries. The Fashion Valley parking garage had 2 to 3 feet of water in the lowest level. The Ward and Fashion Valley trolly centers were surrounded by 1 to 3 feet of water. Water was flowing up to the Riverleaf Inn, mostly blocked by K-rail but was flowing into Hotel circle. Flooded areas were observed as early as 1 pm. Flash flooding along the river including Ward road.

An eucalyptus tree was blown over and blocked all lanes on Sweetwater Road in Bonita. Wind gusts of 30-35 mph were recorded at the time. Severe trees were downed along I-805 and required emergency clean up by Caltrans. Strong winds from a thunderstorm.
All 4 lanes on I-805 North near El Cajon Blvd were flooded.
Flooding and mud debris from construction east of this location were observed.
Two trees were down on the road at SR-163 South and the Washington Street offramp.
CalTrans report of flooding at I-5 South and Main Street.
State Route 98 closed between County Highway 2 and Brockman Road due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported in the area of State Route 111 and East Worthington Road. No damages or injuries were reported.

The New River USGS Gauge at the International Border in Calexico reported water levels peaking to 15.6 feet, which is just above minor flood stage. The rise to minor flood stage was generally gradual as water levels rose at a rate of 1 feet per hour according to the gauge data. The rising water levels caused damage to an improvement project being performed at the New River in Calexico with water overtopping the sheet piles. About 10 feet of standing water was estimated inside the sheet piles. This water overtopping caused a generator controlling the dewatering to flood and shutdown. The city of Calexico declared an emergency due to the damages that the high water levels caused to the project. According to an interview performed with a city councilmember  approximately two weeks after the incident, the damage cost estimate was at around 4 million dollars. No injuries were reported.
Pictures received via social media of flooding on roads in Ocean Beach, specifically on Spray Street near the dog beach.
Report received via social media showing pictures of flooding from Chollas Creek which flooded downstream to Rigel Street. Cars were submerged up to their door handles in the photos.
CalTrans reported the Hawthorn Street off-ramp on I-5 was closed due to flooding.
Flooding reported along East Aten Road between Dogwood Road and State Route 111. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along State Route 86 in the area of Red Earth Casino. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along Highway 177 between Interstate 10 and Highway 62. No damages or injuries reported.
Box Canyon Road closed between Interstate 10 and the All-American Canal due to flooding causing light mud and debris flow. No damages were reported.
CalTrans reported all lanes of Northbound SR-15 south of Ocean View Blvd were closed due to flooding.
Flooding reported along Dunaway Road just south of West Evan Hewes Highway. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video received from social media of a flooded parking lot with water flowing along train tracks in Encanto. The fast flowing water in and around Chollas Creek was strong enough to carry vehicles downstream.
Ogilby Road closed between Interstate 8 and State Route 78 due to overflowing washes causing flooding on the road. No damages or injuries were reported.

The driver of a big rig lost control in heavy rain and hit a guard rail and traveled down an embankment. During recovery of the truck, its fuel tank was punctured, spilling fuel across the roadway and resulting in a full closure of northbound I-15 at I-8.
Avenue A by 28th Street was closed due to a storm drain shooting water up and causing the road to flood. No damages or injuries were reported.
